title: Eurostar staff strike in Paris causes train cancellations

tea.why: Staff are protesting against stagnant wages and restructuring following the 2023 merger with Thalys.
tea.want: Improved wages and a resolution to grievances regarding company restructuring.
tea.changed: Nov 25: Eurostar staff in Paris launched an unannounced strike, leading to multiple train cancellations between Paris, London, and Brussels.

summary: On November 25, 2026, Eurostar staff based in Paris, including train drivers and managers, initiated an unannounced strike, causing significant disruptions to international rail services. The industrial action resulted in the cancellation of several trains between Paris and London, as well as services involving Brussels. According to the CGT Cheminots union, the strike was triggered by a reception held for the departing CEO, which exacerbated tensions over stagnant wages and company restructuring following the 2023 merger with Thalys. Eurostar reported that it was notified of the strike overnight and advised passengers to postpone travel. The company has offered affected passengers the option to rebook or receive a full refund. Eurostar management stated they remain open to constructive dialogue with the unions to resolve the ongoing pay negotiations.
response: Eurostar stated they were notified of the strike overnight and are currently in discussions with the union, expressing a willingness to engage in constructive dialogue.

updates.text: Eurostar staff in Paris began an unannounced strike, causing cancellations on routes between Paris, London, and Brussels.
